name: Groupe BPCE
desc: Co-operative banking group owning Banque Populaire and Caisse d'Epargne networks, plus Natixis wholesale banking.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 25.7bn in 2022 (Wikipedia infobox); USD 78.9bn revenue in 2025 French ranking
markets: France with 8,200+ branches, Belgium via Nagelmackers, Portugal via Novo Banco, wholesale banking abroad
rationale: Rival French banks BNP Paribas and Société Générale court global audiences; F1 could lift Natixis and retail brands internationally.

name: Crédit Mutuel
desc: French co-operative banking group owning CIC, Targobank, Cofidis, Beobank and other retail banking brands.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 57.5bn in 2025 French ranking; EUR 20.4bn revenue in 2022 per Wikipedia
markets: France, Germany (Targobank), Belgium (Beobank), Luxembourg, stakes in Tunisia and Morocco
rationale: Multi-brand bank active in France, Germany and Belgium could use F1 hospitality and reach for CIC and Targobank.

name: Leroy Merlin
desc: DIY and home improvement retail chain, part of Groupe ADEO, owned by the Mulliez family and employees.
markets: France, Spain, Italy, Portugal, Poland, Greece, Romania, Cyprus, Ukraine, China, Brazil, South Africa
rationale: Large multi-country DIY retailer whose tool and hardware rivals (DeWalt, Einhell) already use F1 to reach handy consumers.

name: Kiabi
desc: Low-price family clothing retailer founded by Patrick Mulliez, part of the Mulliez family association.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 2.5bn in 2025 (article body; infobox gives EUR 1.28bn for 2024)
markets: France plus stores in Spain, Italy, Kuwait and other countries, over 30 countries in total
rationale: Mass-market fashion brand expanding abroad; F1's growing family and female audience fits its value fashion positioning.

name: Sodiaal
desc: French dairy co-operative producing Candia milk, Yoplait yoghurts, Entremont cheese and other dairy brands.
markets: Mainly France, with international dairy sales and Yoplait franchise history abroad
rationale: Owner of mass dairy brands Candia and Yop; F1 sponsorship would be a large national consumer marketing play.

name: Agrial
desc: Agricultural co-operative making Florette salads, Loïc Raison cider, Soignon cheese and Maître Jacques meats.
markets: France plus sites in the UK, Spain, Germany, Belgium, Switzerland, Italy, Portugal, Tunisia and the US
rationale: Consumer food brands sold across Europe and the US could gain retailer hospitality and visibility through F1.

name: Terrena
desc: Agri-food co-operative behind Père Dodu poultry, Paysan Breton dairy and Tipiak, through subsidiaries.
markets: France: farming supplies, meat, poultry, dairy and grocery products
rationale: Owns national grocery brands but is a farmer co-operative; F1 would be an unusual but possible brand-building step.

name: Groupe Bigard
desc: Meat processor producing Bigard, Charal and Socopa beef and pork products across around 60 French sites.
markets: France: about 60 industrial sites supplying retail and food service
rationale: Already sponsors top rugby; a family-run meat giant with the Charal consumer brand could use F1 hospitality for retailers.

name: Groupe Bel
desc: Family-controlled cheese maker of The Laughing Cow, Babybel, Kiri and Boursin, plus Pom'Potes fruit snacks.
markets: Sold in more than 120 countries with around 30 factories in about 15 countries
rationale: Global snack-cheese brands like Babybel target families worldwide; F1 can deliver broad international consumer reach.

name: Groupe Even
desc: Breton agri-food co-operative group making Paysan Breton dairy products and running food distribution businesses.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 2.096bn (dairy co-operative table, year not stated)
markets: France, mainly Brittany: dairy, food distribution and farm supply
rationale: Regional co-operative with consumer dairy brands; an F1 deal is unlikely beyond national brand visibility.

name: MAIF
desc: Mutual insurance company serving over four million French members with car, home and personal insurance.
markets: France: car, home, health and personal insurance for 4.1 million members
rationale: Large car insurer with a mass motorist customer base; F1's French audience growth gives marketing relevance.

name: Lesaffre
desc: Family-owned producer of baker's yeast and fermentation ingredients, with 95 subsidiaries in 55 countries.
markets: 95 subsidiaries in 55 countries supplying bakers, food makers and industry
rationale: Mostly business-to-business yeast supplier; F1 would serve customer hospitality with global bakers rather than consumer branding.

name: AG2R La Mondiale
desc: Mutual and joint social-protection group providing life insurance, pensions, health cover and savings in France.
sponsorships: Cycling team sponsor 1997-2025; Transat AG2R sailing race 1995-2020; French road races from 2026
markets: France: pensions, life, health and savings for individuals and employers
rationale: A seasoned sports sponsor that just left pro cycling and is looking for new sports platforms.

name: Pierre Fabre
desc: Pharmaceutical and dermo-cosmetics group, 86% owned by the Fondation Pierre Fabre, making Avène and Klorane products.
markets: Products distributed in 116 countries; 71% of revenue earned outside France
rationale: Avène and Klorane are global skincare brands; rival cosmetics firms (SkinCeuticals) already use F1 for reach.

name: Servier
desc: Pharmaceutical group wholly owned by the Fondation Servier, selling medicines in nearly 140 countries.
markets: Present in nearly 140 countries worldwide, with headquarters and research in France
rationale: Prescription drug maker with limited consumer marketing; F1 would mainly serve corporate image and recruiting.

name: Groupe Rocher
desc: Family-controlled beauty group owning Yves Rocher, Dr Pierre Ricaud, Sabon and Arbonne cosmetics brands.
markets: Present in 118 countries with about 2,500 stores, online, direct and mail-order sales
rationale: International beauty brands seeking younger customers; F1's growing female audience is a fit, as rivals like ELEMIS show.

name: Castel Group
industry: wine, beer and soft drinks group
desc: Family-owned drinks group making French wines, Nicolas wine shops and beers like 33 Export in Africa.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 5.6bn in 2019 (financial table; infobox estimates EUR 6.5bn for 2024)
markets: France for wines and Nicolas shops; Africa (Cameroon, Côte d'Ivoire, Morocco, Madagascar and more) for over 80% of sales
rationale: Major drinks group whose rivals Heineken and Moët Hennessy use F1; could build its beer brands across Africa.

name: Grands Chais de France
desc: Wine producer behind J.P. Chenet, Calvet and Arthur Metz, exporting about 80% of its sales.
markets: France plus Germany, Spain, Italy, Hungary, China, the US and Japan; about 80% of revenue from exports
rationale: Export-led wine brand J.P. Chenet could use F1's global hospitality, as Champagne houses already do.

name: Lyreco
desc: Business-to-business distributor of office and workplace supplies, present in 44 countries in 2014.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 548m in 2024 (French entity); EUR 2bn consolidated in 2014
markets: 44 countries in 2014; market leader in France and Spain
rationale: B2B supplier to large companies; F1 hospitality could support key-account sales rather than consumer branding.

name: Mobivia
industry: car maintenance and parts retail group
desc: Family-owned group running Norauto, Midas, A.T.U and Carter-Cash car servicing and auto parts networks.
markets: 17 countries incl. France, Germany, Portugal, Spain and Italy; 410 Norauto centres in France
rationale: Car servicing brands talk to motorists; F1 fits naturally, as rival aftermarket brands like Armor All and Motul show.

name: Conforama
desc: Furniture, home appliances and decoration retailer owned by Mobilux, a venture of XXXLutz and CD&R.
sponsorships: Ligue 1 title sponsor ('Ligue 1 Conforama') from 2017 for three seasons
markets: France plus stores in Luxembourg, Switzerland, Italy, Spain, Portugal and New Caledonia
rationale: Former Ligue 1 title sponsor used to big sports deals; F1's rising French audience could revive that strategy.

name: Kiloutou
desc: Equipment and tool rental company for builders and businesses, controlled by the Dentressangle family holding.
markets: France, renting construction equipment and tools from a branch network
rationale: Mainly B2B rental; F1 could serve customer hospitality but brand fit is limited.

name: Mane
desc: Family-run maker of flavours and fragrances for food, perfume and consumer goods companies, present in 39 countries.
markets: Present in 39 countries, supplying food, beverage, perfume and household product makers
rationale: B2B ingredients supplier; F1 would serve client hospitality and employer branding more than consumer reach.

name: Groupe Amaury
desc: Family-owned group publishing L'Équipe and running Amaury Sport Organisation, organiser of the Tour de France and Dakar.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 680m in 2014 (article body; infobox shows holding figure EUR 30.8m for 2024)
sponsorships: Organiser of Tour de France and Dakar Rally via ASO
markets: France-based media; sports events and operations in about 25 countries
rationale: Sports media owner with L'Équipe and Dakar motorsport rally; a media or content partnership with F1 is conceivable.

name: Brittany Ferries
desc: Ferry company running passenger and freight routes between France, the UK, Ireland and Spain.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 441.8m in year to 31 October 2018
markets: France, United Kingdom, Ireland and Spain across 12 ferry routes
rationale: Carries British and Irish motorists to France; F1 hospitality and fan travel tie-ins around European races could fit.

name: Groupe Beaumanoir
desc: Family fashion group owning Cache-Cache, Bonobo, Morgan, La Halle, Caroll and Sarenza, with 1,700 stores.
markets: 1,255 stores in France and 440 abroad (2023); Quiksilver and Billabong licences in Western Europe
rationale: Multi-brand fashion retailer; F1's younger audience could suit brands like Bonobo, though focus remains France.

name: La Martiniquaise
desc: Spirits producer owned by COFEPP, making Label 5 and Cutty Sark whisky, Poliakov vodka and Porto Cruz.
markets: France plus distilleries and brands in Scotland, the Netherlands, Belgium, Italy, Portugal and Réunion; exports
rationale: Whisky and spirits rivals (Chivas, Glenfiddich, Jack Daniel's) are F1 partners; Cutty Sark or Label 5 could follow.

name: Groupe Éram
desc: Family-founded footwear and fashion group running Éram, Bocage, Gémo, Mellow Yellow and TBS chains.
markets: France, through Éram, Gémo and other store chains
rationale: Mainly a French mass-market retailer; F1 relevance limited to domestic brand building.

name: Swinkels Family Brewers
desc: Seventh-generation family brewer of Bavaria, La Trappe, Rodenbach and Swinckels' beers sold in over 130 countries.
markets: More than 130 countries, including Ethiopia where it brews Negus malt drink
rationale: Bavaria 0.0 competes with Heineken, an F1 partner; Dutch F1 fan boom offers a direct home-market fit.

name: Van Oord
desc: Privately held Dutch marine contractor for dredging, offshore wind installation and coastal infrastructure worldwide.
markets: Offices in about 33 countries across Europe, the Americas, Asia, Australia and the Middle East
rationale: B2B marine contractor; F1 hospitality could support client relations in Gulf and Asian markets hosting Grands Prix.

name: Damen Shipyards
desc: Family-owned shipbuilding group designing and building tugs, ferries, naval and offshore vessels and yachts.
markets: Doing business in 120 countries with yards in Europe and elsewhere
rationale: Builds superyachts through its group; F1's wealthy paddock audience could suit yacht and premium vessel sales.

name: Pon Holdings
desc: Family-owned mobility group owning Gazelle, Cannondale, Cervélo and Santa Cruz bikes plus vehicle import businesses.
markets: Netherlands, United States, China, Norway and other markets for bikes, cars and equipment
rationale: World's leading bike group and long-time Volkswagen-group importer; F1 could showcase its performance cycling brands.

name: Jumbo
desc: Dutch supermarket chain owned by the Van Eerd family, operating stores in the Netherlands and Flanders.
sponsorships: Max Verstappen personal sponsor to 2023; Team Jumbo-Visma cycling 2013-2023/24; skating team 2014-2023; Racing Team Nederland WEC 2018-2020
markets: Supermarkets across the Netherlands and in Belgium (Flanders), with online grocery sales
rationale: Former Verstappen sponsor with deep motorsport experience; could return to F1 to reach the large Dutch fan base.

name: HEMA
desc: Dutch variety store chain selling own-brand household goods, clothing and food, owned by the Van Eerd family.
markets: Almost 750 stores in the Netherlands, Belgium, Germany, France, Austria, Luxembourg and franchise markets
rationale: New owner Van Eerd family previously sponsored Verstappen through Jumbo; HEMA could carry similar Dutch fan marketing.

name: C&A
desc: Family-owned fashion retailer with about 1,400 European stores, owned by the Brenninkmeijer family through Cofra.
markets: 18 European countries, core market Germany with about 450 stores; Brazil unit listed separately
rationale: Mass fashion brand with past World Cup sponsorship; F1's young and female fan growth matches its family apparel market.

name: Vion Food Group
desc: Meat processor with pork and beef production sites in the Netherlands, Germany and Belgium, owned by farmers.
markets: Production in the Netherlands, Germany and Belgium; sales locations on all continents
rationale: Mainly a B2B meat supplier to retailers; F1 fit is weak beyond customer hospitality in Europe.

name: Puratos
desc: Family-owned maker of bakery, patisserie and chocolate ingredients with subsidiaries in 68 countries.
markets: Subsidiaries in 68 countries; over 55 factories in 43 countries (2018)
rationale: Mainly B2B ingredients; F1 hospitality could serve large bakery and food-service clients worldwide.

name: BCD Travel
desc: Corporate travel management company owned by the Fentener van Vlissingen family, operating in 170-plus countries.
markets: Operates in more than 170 countries for corporate clients
rationale: Serves global corporations whose executives attend Grands Prix; F1 hospitality and travel logistics are a natural link.

name: De Heus
desc: Fourth-generation family-owned animal feed producer selling in 75 countries with subsidiaries across four continents.
markets: 75 countries; subsidiaries in Poland, Ukraine, Spain, Egypt, Ethiopia, South Africa, Vietnam, Brazil and more
rationale: B2B feed maker with farmer customers; F1 would mainly serve corporate image in emerging markets.

name: Intergamma
desc: Parent of the Gamma and Karwei DIY store chains with 381 stores in the Netherlands and Belgium.
markets: Netherlands and Belgium (Gamma in both, Karwei in the Netherlands)
rationale: DIY chain in the F1-mad Dutch market; tool brands already in F1 show the category's fit with motorsport fans.

name: Rituals
desc: Dutch cosmetics and home fragrance brand selling through more than 1,400 own stores in 33 countries.
markets: More than 1,400 own stores in 33 countries, plus online sales across Europe and beyond
rationale: Fast-growing premium beauty brand from the Netherlands; F1's growing female audience and Dutch fan base fit well.

name: Royal Cosun
desc: Farmers' co-operative owning Cosun Beet Company sugar, Aviko potato products, Sensus inulin and Duynie feed businesses.
markets: Netherlands, Belgium, Germany, Poland, Spain and the US; 63% of revenue from Europe outside the Netherlands
rationale: Aviko fries reach food-service chains worldwide; F1 would be mainly a B2B hospitality and brand platform.

name: Agrifirm
desc: Dutch agricultural co-operative supplying animal feed, crop inputs and advice to farmers across Europe and beyond.
markets: Netherlands plus Belgium, Germany, France, Spain, Romania, Hungary, Poland, Serbia, Ukraine, Uruguay, Brazil and China
rationale: Farmer-facing co-operative with little consumer branding; F1 relevance is low beyond corporate hospitality.

name: Avebe
desc: Farmers' co-operative producing potato starch and protein ingredients for food, paper and industrial uses.
markets: Production in the Netherlands, Germany and Sweden; about half of revenue from outside the EU
rationale: B2B potato starch ingredient maker; F1 would only serve client hospitality, not consumer marketing.

name: DELA
desc: Non-profit co-operative providing funeral insurance and funeral services in the Netherlands, Belgium and Germany.
markets: Netherlands, Belgium (Antwerp) and Germany (Düsseldorf); 5.6 million insured
rationale: Funeral insurance brand with a sombre category; F1 sponsorship fit is weak.

name: Univé
desc: Dutch co-operative insurer for car, home and health cover, owned by about 1.6 million members.
capacity_detail: Official sponsor of PSV and partner of Feyenoord, both clubs playing in the UEFA Champions League
sponsorships: PSV (official sponsor), Feyenoord, FC Twente, FC Groningen and other Eredivisie clubs; Amstel Gold Race; NOS Studio Sport
markets: Netherlands, through eight regional branches and about 1.6 million co-operative members
rationale: Heavy Dutch sports sponsor and car insurer; F1's huge Dutch audience suits its football-led marketing.

name: Heerema Marine Contractors
desc: Offshore contractor using heavy-lift crane vessels to install oil, gas and wind energy structures at sea.
markets: Projects worldwide including the North Sea, Angola, Norway and Asia; offices in Leiden, Geneva, Luxembourg
rationale: B2B offshore contractor; F1 fit is limited to hospitality for energy clients in Grand Prix host markets.

name: DPG Media
industry: news, TV and radio media group
desc: Family-controlled media group owning VTM, RTL Nederland, Het Laatste Nieuws, de Volkskrant, AD and NU.nl.
markets: Belgium (Flanders, plus stakes in Wallonia and Brussels) and the Netherlands; Danish arm being sold
rationale: Owns RTL Nederland and Videoland in Verstappen's home market; a media or content partnership with F1 is plausible.

name: Mediahuis
desc: Family-owned news publisher of De Standaard, De Telegraaf, NRC, Irish Independent and Luxemburger Wort.
markets: Belgium, the Netherlands, Ireland and Northern Ireland, Germany and Luxembourg
rationale: Publishes De Telegraaf, a major Dutch F1 news outlet; media partnership or hospitality could suit its reader marketing.

name: H.Essers
desc: Family-owned transport and logistics group with 85 locations in 19 European countries, specialising in pharma logistics.
sponsorships: Formerly sponsored cyclist Sven Nys (via KDL)
markets: 85 locations in 19 countries across Western and Eastern Europe
rationale: Logistics peers DHL and CEVA are F1 partners; a smaller trackside or hospitality deal could raise its European profile.

name: Cactus
desc: Family-owned Luxembourg supermarket and retail group run by the Leesch family since 1900.
markets: Luxembourg, through supermarkets and retail outlets run from its Bertrange head office
rationale: Leading Luxembourg grocer; F1 would be a domestic brand-building play with limited reach benefit.

name: Groupe VYV
desc: Mutual health and social protection group uniting MGEN, Harmonie Mutuelle and other French mutual insurers.
markets: France: health insurance, care services and housing through affiliated mutuals
rationale: France's largest health mutual; F1 offers national brand visibility, but health-insurer fit with motorsport is modest.

name: Brioche Pasquier
desc: Family-controlled maker of brioches, pains au lait and baked goods, delisted from the Paris Bourse in 2006.
sponsorships: Official supplier to the France football team at the 2018 FIFA World Cup
markets: France plus factories in Spain, Portugal, the United Kingdom and the United States
rationale: Has sponsored national football; a family snack brand expanding in the UK and US could use F1 for awareness.

name: Maïsadour
desc: Southwest French farm co-operative owning Delpeyrat foie gras, St Sever poultry and MAS Seeds.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 1.344bn in year to June 2019
markets: France; MAS Seeds active in Germany, Italy, Spain, Poland, Romania, Ukraine and Turkey
rationale: Farm co-operative with gourmet brands; F1 relevance limited to luxury food hospitality.

name: Euralis
desc: Agricultural co-operative producing Maison Montfort and Rougié foie gras, seeds and ready-made food, in 16 countries.
markets: Present in 16 countries, with foie gras, seeds and ready-made food sold in France and abroad
rationale: Rougié supplies top restaurants; F1 Paddock Club catering is a niche link, but overall fit is weak.

name: Lur Berri
desc: Basque farm co-operative with meat processing, holding stakes in Labeyrie Fine Foods and Spanghero.
markets: Southwest France: Pyrénées-Atlantiques, Landes, Hautes-Pyrénées and Haute-Garonne departments
rationale: Regional farm co-operative with limited consumer branding; F1 fit is low beyond its Labeyrie stake.

name: Groupe Barrière
desc: Family-owned operator of 34 casinos and 18 luxury hotels including Fouquet's, mainly in France.
markets: France plus Switzerland, Morocco, Egypt, Côte d'Ivoire, Saint-Barthélemy and the United States (Fouquet's New York)
rationale: Casino-resort peers MGM, Wynn, Caesars and Hard Rock are F1 partners; Barrière could follow in Europe.

name: Groupe Le Duff
desc: Family-founded group running Brioche Dorée, Del Arte and La Madeleine restaurants plus Bridor bakery products.
markets: 1,958 restaurants and bakeries in 90 countries across five continents
rationale: International café and bakery chains in 90 countries; F1 race-weekend catering and global reach could suit it.

name: Groupe Bertrand
desc: Founder-led restaurant group running Burger King France, Hippopotamus, Au Bureau, Angelina and Brasserie Lipp.
markets: France and Belgium mainly, with Angelina in Dubai, China, Hong Kong and Doha
rationale: Large French consumer food operator; Burger King France and Angelina could leverage F1 for youth and luxury audiences.

name: Fimalac
desc: Holding of Marc Ladreit de Lacharrière owning Webedia, Allociné and live entertainment venues, delisted in 2017.
markets: France, with Webedia in Germany, Spain, Brazil, Turkey, Middle East, plus US, UK and Asia
rationale: Webedia runs gaming and creator media; F1 content partnerships could fit, but sponsorship spending is uncertain.
